en.headline: Teen arrested over two Guess Who I Am scams totalling 410,000
en.dek: Kwun Tong police said a 17-year-old collected cash after two elderly residents were told a relative needed bail money, in cases reported in July.
body: Kwun Tong police arrested a 17-year-old local youth on Thursday on suspicion of obtaining property by deception, after two "Guess Who I Am" telephone scams in July that cost two elderly residents a total of about 410,000 dollars.

Inspector Sze Wah-sing of Kwun Tong District Crime Squad 3 said fraudsters first rang older people at random, posing as relatives or friends who claimed they had been detained in a criminal case and needed bail money. A second caller then posed as a friend sent to collect the cash, and arranged to meet near Lei Yue Mun in Kwun Tong.

The victims, aged 74 and 89, handed over the money and later reached their real relatives, then reported the deception. Officers used closed-circuit television under the Eyes in the Sky scheme to identify the person who collected the cash, and arrested the youth, who is unemployed, on Thursday. He was being held for further inquiries.

Police advised older people who receive unexpected calls asking for money to stay calm and check directly with family, or call the Anti-Scam Helpline 18222. Obtaining property by deception carries a maximum sentence of 10 years' imprisonment.

zh.headline: 觀塘兩宗猜猜我是誰騙案 17歲青年涉收款被捕
zh.dek: 警方周四拘捕一名17歲本地青年，涉嫌在7月兩宗電話騙案中向兩名長者收取合共約41萬元「保釋金」。
body: 觀塘警方周四以「以欺騙手段取得財產」罪名拘捕一名17歲本地青年，案件涉及今年7月兩宗「猜猜我是誰」電話騙案，兩名長者合共損失約41萬元。
觀塘警區刑事調查隊第三隊督察施華聖表示，騙徒先隨機致電長者，訛稱是其親人或朋友因刑事案件被拘留，需要繳付保釋金，其後再冒充親友的朋友，約定在觀塘鯉魚門一帶收取現金。
兩名事主分別74歲及89歲，付款後成功聯絡真正親人，發現受騙後報警。警方透過「銳眼」計劃翻查閉路電視鎖定收款人，周四將報稱無業的該名青年拘捕，現正扣留調查。
警方呼籲長者接獲陌生人來電索款時先保持冷靜，直接向親友核實，或致電防騙易18222查詢。以欺騙手段取得財產最高可判監禁10年。
